newsitem.title: UK: UK March-May primary fuel use falls 9.2 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: UK March-May primary fuel use falls 9.2 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Britain's primary fuel consumption from March to May this year was 9.2 percent lower than the same period in 1996, preliminary figures from the Department of Trade and Industry showed on Tuesday.
Total consumption was 54.5 million tonnes of oil equivalent.
Petroleum consumption fell by 4.9 percent to 20.2 million tonnes.

The DTI said a fall in fuel oil deliveries by 40.3 percent was due to "the conversion of Premier Power's Northern Ireland power station to gas and to a general move away by the industry from using fuel oil as a source of energy."
Deliveries to the petrochemical industry were down 12.5 percent, with deliveries of petroleum coke to the industrial sector down by 19 percent.
Coal consumption fell by 23.3 percent, mainly as a result of declining use at power stations, the DTI said.
Demand for natural gas fell by 9.8 percent, while primary electricity consumption increased by 7.4 percent.
